?

Using the method of orthogonal transformations, find the canonical form of Q(x)=2x12+2x22+2x32+6x1x2.

a
5y12+2y22−y32
b
2y12+2y22+y32
c
4y12−2y22+2y32
d
3y12+5y22−y32
e
3y12−2y22−y32
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

A=[230320002]

Every quadratic form can be reduced to its canonical (diagonal) form using orthogonal transformations.

To find the coefficients of the canonical form, we need to calculate the eigenvalues of A:

|A−λI|=0|2−λ3032−λ0002−λ|=0(2−λ)|2−λ332−λ|=0(2−λ)((2−λ)(2−λ)−9)=0(2−λ)(λ2−4λ−5)=0(2−λ)(λ−5)(λ+1)=0λ=5,2,−1

So, writing the eigenvalues in descending order, we obtain the diagonal matrix

D=[50002000−1].

The corresponding quadratic form after a change of variables is

5y12+2y22−y32.

EXPLANATION

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

A=[9226]

Every quadratic form can be reduced to its canonical (diagonal) form using orthogonal transformations.

To find the coefficients of the canonical form, we need to calculate the eigenvalues of A:

|A−λI|=0|9−λ226−λ|=0λ2−15λ+50=0λ=10,5

Now, we need to find an eigenvector basis of A.

  • For λ1=10, we have A−10I=[9226]−10[1001]=[−122−4]. Seeking a non-zero solution of (A−10I)x=0 gives the eigenvector v1=[21]. Dividing v1 by its norm ‖v1‖=5, we get v1‖v1‖=15[21]=[2515].

Finally, we construct the diagonal matrix D (writing the eigenvalues in descending order) and the orthogonal matrix P in the usual way, and this gives us the following: D=[10005],P=[25−151525]
